scope.method: Read existing sanitized R4 artifact, graph-first discovery, targeted current runtime and installed Pi SDK source inspection. No live request issued.

evidence.label: reply-terminal-foundation-check
evidence.eventClock: Database created_at, not raw local tool start/end or provider latency
evidence.graph: runBuilder graph exists but line ranges are stale; Coordinator/output/workspace gaps inspected directly after graph returned insufficient results

observedToolIntervals.definition: tool.started to tool.completed includes event persistence, active-role checks and remote operations. These are NOT isolated model or command execution durations.

rankedCandidates.name: Serial persistence barriers around every tool
rankedCandidates.chain: Builder awaits tool.start -> remote operation -> output.finish/drain -> tool.end before Pi sees the tool result and can request the next model turn. Coordinator normally awaits active -> start event -> in-memory domain work -> active -> end event; final decision also awaits active and onDecision.
rankedCandidates.evidence: 11 Builder tool intervals total 200215ms. Ten output-to-completed gaps total 71292ms (3509–12095ms each); even three Coordinator tools total 26082ms although their business work is in memory.
rankedCandidates.measurement: Measure each onEvent callback and assertActive duration independently, then compare same-demand run after API/DB co-location. Keep durable event ordering and fail-closed barriers.

rankedCandidates.name: Multiple serial remote calls for each small file operation
rankedCandidates.chain: read/write uploads one staging JSON, starts a background source-io process, fetches logs, checks status, then fetches final logs. Minimum five sequential sandbox API operations for a short completed read/write; edit performs one read plus one write (minimum ten), plus local diff generation. Bash has minimum four command API operations. Additional polling adds logs/status pairs and 180ms delays.
rankedCandidates.measurement: Separate staging-upload, command-start, polling and final-drain elapsed times; compare local API-to-sandbox RTT after co-location. No per-operation timing exists in R4 artifact.

rankedCandidates.name: Template initialization before Builder tracker/model starts
rankedCandidates.chain: Sandbox create/register/renew -> setup command -> upload/chmod helper -> six serial template writes -> two commands to read baked package/lock -> two further writes. At the current facade this is at least 57 sandbox API operations for initialization when each short command finishes in its first status poll, excluding create/renew and database registration.
rankedCandidates.evidence: Builder role start to first recorded stream event is 74764ms. Role wall time exceeds the runtime tracker by 78383.941542ms; this includes pre-Pi setup and post-runtime terminal persistence/cleanup and cannot all be assigned to initialization.
rankedCandidates.measurement: Time create/register/renew and initializeReactWorkspace separately before runBuilder; retain the same trusted template and ownership checks.

rankedCandidates.name: Provider response callback can gate stream consumption
rankedCandidates.chain: Installed Pi awaits onResponse before emitting start/consuming SSE. Builder onResponse awaits emit(stage). First delta schedules a fixed stream-start event without directly awaiting it, but the next awaited tool.start must drain that eventTail. Pi awaits the tool batch before the next model request.
rankedCandidates.measurement: Record response-header time, onResponse callback duration and first delta separately; inspect whether the parent event adapter persists or drops stage events. R4 totals (Coordinator 3 model calls/2050 output tokens, Builder 9/3189) are not model-only timings.

excludedConclusions: The 250ms output timer is a maximum flush interval, not a mandatory 250ms sleep per tool; finish flushes immediately.
No evidence supports attributing the 6–26s tool spans solely to the model, shell or gVisor CPU.
No individual provider latency, remote command CPU time or active-role callback duration was measured by this report.
No claim that co-location already improved latency; it requires a new comparable real run.
